claim: Perfect classification accuracy (F1=1.00) on SGCC dataset
evidence: REAL_SGCC_BASELINE_RESULTS.csv demonstrates real SGCC F1 is 0.401-0.416, not 1.00.
recommended_neutral_wording: The legacy synthetic dataset produced artificial F1=1.00 due to deterministic zero injection. Real SGCC evaluation yields Test F1 = 0.4014 - 0.4161.

claim: The 18-feature model is universally superior to the 42-feature model
evidence: Full 42-feature model achieves Test F1 = 0.4161 vs 18-feature Test F1 = 0.4014.
recommended_neutral_wording: The 18-feature model offers comparable performance (Test F1 = 0.4014 vs 0.4161) with 57% fewer features and improved noise resilience, presenting a performance-complexity tradeoff.

evidence: Missingness features (missing_streak_count, missing_count) rank #1 in SHAP importance, but missingness reflects telecommunication drops as well as physical tampering.
recommended_neutral_wording: Missingness features exhibit strong predictive association (SHAP importance) with theft flags without establishing direct physical causality.

claim: GridBalance is a production-ready smart grid system
evidence: Evaluated on historical datasets without live utility deployment, operational cost calibration, or concept drift monitoring.
recommended_neutral_wording: GridBalance is a research-grade prototype demonstration integrating frozen ML models with a FastAPI inference engine and React dashboard.

claim: UCI Load Forecaster achieves 0.9944 R^2 and 1.93% sMAPE
evidence: Sealed test evaluation on H2 2014 load data confirms MAE = 4,421.55 kWh, RMSE = 6,654.94 kWh, R^2 = 0.9944, sMAPE = 1.93%.
recommended_neutral_wording: The frozen XGBoost regressor achieves an R^2 of 0.9944 and sMAPE of 1.93% on the sealed 6-month aggregate load test set.

claim: Synthetic evasion experiments evaluate real-world physical meter bypass
evidence: Evasion experiments simulate mathematical load scaling (x'_t = alpha * x_t), which does not capture all physical bypass hardware interventions.
recommended_neutral_wording: Controlled evasion simulations evaluate model sensitivity to multiplicative load scaling, representing a mathematical approximation of theft evasion.
